BohrSet.statement: For an additive commutative group $G$, $\mathrm{BohrSet}(G)$ is the type (in the same universe as $G$) of structures $B$ consisting of: a finite set $\mathrm{frequencies}(B)$ of additive characters $\psi : G\to\mathbb{C}$ (homomorphisms from the additive group $G$ to the multiplicative monoid of $\mathbb{C}$); a function $\mathrm{ewidth}_B$ assigning to every additive character $\psi : G\to\mathbb{C}$ (not only to the frequencies) an extended nonnegative real number $\mathrm{ewidth}_B(\psi)\in[0,\infty]$; and the condition that for every additive character $\psi : G\to\mathbb{C}$, $\psi\in\mathrm{frequencies}(B)$ if and only if $\mathrm{ewidth}_B(\psi)<\infty$. According to its docstring, $\mathrm{ewidth}_B(\psi)$ is called the width of $B$ at $\psi$, and $B$ is thought of as the set $\{x\in G : \|1-\psi(x)\|\le \mathrm{width}_B(\psi)\text{ for all }\psi\in\mathrm{frequencies}(B)\}$ (the chord-length convention, as opposed to the arc-length convention $|\arg\psi(x)|\le\mathrm{width}_B(\psi)$); this set does not uniquely determine $B$ (neither its frequencies nor its widths).
